question: Um, what average does my son need to get into one of the engineering technology diplomas?
expected_answer: At least 62 percent overall in his top six Grade 12 courses, plus Grade 12 English and Grade 12 mathematics at 60 percent or higher.

meta.note: Distractor: the degree requirements doc says 72 percent.

question: And would that one need any particular science courses, or is it just the average?
expected_answer: Practical Nursing needs Grade 12 Biology at 65 percent or higher and Grade 11 Chemistry at 60 percent or higher, on top of the 62 percent average and Grade 12 English.

history.content: Hi, my daughter's thinking about applying for the practical nursing diploma.
That's a popular programme. What would you like to know about it?

question: How much longer does a bachelor's degree take than a two year college diploma?
expected_answer: Usually about two years longer: a bachelor's degree is typically four years of full-time study, while a college diploma is typically two.

question: What overall score do I actually need on the English test if I'm applying for a diploma?
expected_answer: On an approved nine-band academic test you need 5.5 overall with no band below 5.0, or 60 out of 120 on an approved internet-based test.

meta.note: Superseded March 2024 rules required 6.0 with no band below 5.5.

question: If I retake the English test, should all my band scores come from that one new sitting?
expected_answer: No. Band scores from two sittings of the same approved test taken within six months of each other can be combined, using your best score in each band.

key_facts: within six months of each other
meta.note: Common norm: all band scores must come from a single test sitting (no superscoring).

question: Should I take the academic or the general version of the English test for college?
expected_answer: Take the academic version; colleges and universities ask for academic English test results, while the general version is meant for work and migration purposes.

question: How much is the application fee for international students, and do you allow more than one programme?
expected_answer: It's $150 for international applicants, non-refundable, and one application covers up to three programme choices.

meta.note: Superseded 2026-27 rules: $125 and one programme choice only.

question: It's already March, so what does that mean, have I missed the September deadline?
expected_answer: It depends on the programme: most diplomas use rolling admission and stay open until full, but degrees and Practical Nursing had a fixed 1 February 2027 deadline (late files only if seats remain), and international applicants must apply by 1 May 2027.

meta.note: Generic answer (deadlines vary, many colleges are rolling) is plausible but misses the programme-specific dates.

question: Sorry, with rolling admission, should I expect them to decide on people as they apply?
expected_answer: Yes: applications are reviewed as they come in and decisions go out on a running basis until the programme is full, so applying early improves your chances.

history.content: I'm looking at a couple of the diploma programmes for next fall.
Great, I can help with that. Most of the diplomas use rolling admission.

question: If I pay the deposit before the summer and then change my mind, it's non-refundable, right?
expected_answer: Not necessarily: the $500 confirmation deposit is fully refundable if you withdraw your acceptance in writing before 1 July for a September start (1 November for January); after that it's non-refundable.

meta.note: Common norm: a deposit to secure a place is non-refundable.

question: What does accepting my offer actually mean, like how much do I pay and by when?
expected_answer: You confirm by paying a $500 confirmation deposit within 30 days of the offer date, and it's credited in full to your first-term tuition.

key_facts: within 30 days of the offer date
meta.note: International applicants pay a $6,000 tuition deposit instead (intl-01).

question: Before I accept a conditional offer, um, what kind of conditions does it come with?
expected_answer: Usually that you finish your current courses with final grades at or above the required level and send official final transcripts by a set date, plus any outstanding documents such as an English test result.

question: Should I just defer my diploma offer for a year, since I want to work first?
expected_answer: You can't: offers to diploma programmes cannot be deferred, so you'd have to decline, reapply later and pay the application fee again, with no guarantee of admission.

key_facts: Offers to diploma programmes cannot be deferred
meta.note: Common norm: an offer can be deferred for one year on request.

question: My study permit hasn't come through, can I defer my offer to the next intake?
expected_answer: Yes, once: if your study permit isn't approved in time you can defer to the next intake of the same programme at no cost, even for a diploma, and your deposit is held.

history.content: I'm coming from overseas for the September diploma intake.
Welcome! How can I help with your plans?

key_facts: defer once to the next intake
meta.note: Generic 'you can usually request a deferral' is plausible, but the once-only, free, deposit-held rule (and the contrast with domestic diploma offers) is org specific.

question: So is deferring an offer actually the same thing as turning it down?
expected_answer: No. Deferring keeps your place and moves your start to a later intake, while declining gives the place up completely.

question: Do you guys need my overseas transcripts evaluated by an outside credential agency first?
expected_answer: No. All international credentials are evaluated in-house, free of charge, so an outside credential evaluation report is not required; just upload your transcripts, with certified English translations if needed.

meta.note: Common norm: international applicants must supply a credential evaluation report from an external agency.

question: Um, how long after paying the tuition deposit before I get the acceptance letter for my visa?
expected_answer: The letter of acceptance is issued within 10 business days after your $6,000 tuition deposit clears.

question: Do translators charge a fee for transcripts, or can a friend just translate them?
expected_answer: Yes, certified translators normally charge a fee, and a translation by a friend or yourself usually isn't accepted; it has to be a certified translation.

question: How do I split my tuition into instalments with you guys, and is there a fee?
expected_answer: Domestic students can pay each term in three instalments (at registration, 15 October and 15 November for fall) for a $40 plan fee per term, with no interest.

meta.note: International students can only use the plan from their second term.

question: My tuition wire transfer still hasn't shown up after three days, that's okay, right?
expected_answer: Yes, international wire transfers commonly take about two to five business days; if it's longer, ask your bank for the transfer reference or trace number.

question: If I drop out in the first week of classes, I'll get all my tuition back, right?
expected_answer: No. Only withdrawals before the first day of classes get 100 percent; during the first week of classes you get 70 percent of the term's tuition back.

key_facts: before the first day of classes
meta.note: Common norm: a full tuition refund during the first week or add/drop period.

question: Yeah, it's the second week now, so how do I work out what I'd get back?
expected_answer: Withdrawing during the second week gets you 50 percent of the term's tuition, and ancillary fees are refunded in full up to the end of week two; submit the form in the student portal, as that date counts.

history.content: I'm thinking of withdrawing from my programme this term.
I'm sorry to hear that. Have classes already started for you?

question: If my tuition's four thousand dollars and I get seventy percent back, how much would that be?
expected_answer: $2,800, since 70 percent of $4,000 is $2,800.

question: What average would I need for, like, an entrance scholarship, and how much would it be?
expected_answer: It's automatic for domestic applicants: an 85 to 89.9 percent average gets $1,500 and 90 percent or higher gets $2,500.

question: Will I have to pay back a bursary I get, like I would with a loan?
expected_answer: No, a bursary is non-repayable money awarded on financial need; unlike a loan, you don't pay it back.

question: How much do you charge to challenge a course through prior learning assessment?
expected_answer: It's $120 per course, paid before the assessment is booked, and it isn't refunded if you're unsuccessful.

question: I did some college courses about eight years ago, will those still transfer over or not?
expected_answer: Partly: programme-specific courses must be within the last 7 years, so those won't count, but general education courses like English or psychology are accepted within the last 10 years if you got a C or better.

meta.note: Generic answer (credits may expire, depends on the course) is plausible; the 7 vs 10 year split is org specific.

question: How do I put together a prior learning portfolio, what do you guys want to see?
expected_answer: Gather evidence that maps your experience to the course learning outcomes: a resume, job descriptions, certificates, samples of your work and reference letters.

question: If I leave residence at Christmas, will I still owe for the whole year or not?
expected_answer: No. Residence agreements are signed one term at a time; if you give written notice by 15 November you can leave at the end of fall and owe nothing for winter.

meta.note: Common norm: residence contracts bind you for the full academic year with penalties for leaving early.

question: Yeah, what do you suggest if my roommate keeps me up really late every night?
expected_answer: Talk to your roommate calmly first and agree on quiet hours; if that doesn't work, ask your residence assistant to help mediate.

That sounds exciting. Is there anything you're worried about?
